facts.name: New England Aster
facts.notes: A tall fall bloomer covered in purple daisies that feed migrating monarchs. Pinch back by half in early June for a bushier plant.

sources.title: Michigan Wildflower Farm: Dryland species list
sources.note: Michigan seed grower; marks any species that is not native to Michigan.

sources.title: Michigan Wildflower Farm: Wetland species list

companions.why: Plant at the edge of a meadow with butterfly weed and New England aster.
Pair with fall aster, bugbane, eupatorium, goldenrod, sedum or toad lily; near bleeding heart; with variegated hosta and grasses.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Japanese Anemone article

companions.why: Pair with dark-leaved Heuchera; combine with aster, tall sedums like 'Autumn Joy', yarrow, rudbeckias and purple coneflower.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Little Bluestem article

companions.why: Combines well with ornamental grasses, anise hyssop, beebalm, daylilies, fall asters, liatris, purple coneflower and rudbeckias.
